findings.rule: On a successful parse the program writes EXACTLY "<Schema: ['id', 'price', 'tags', 'title']>\n" (43 bytes) to stdout, nothing to stderr, exit 0. The value of --a is never used or echoed; every accepted value produces byte-identical output.
findings.evidence: `--a hello`, `--a=v`, `--a=`, `--a -1`, `--a ''`, `--a 'héllo→'`, `--a $'a\nb'` all -> exit 0, stdout 43 bytes, od -c: `<   S   c   h   e   m   a   :       [   '   i   d   '   , ...`

findings.rule: prog = basename(argv[0]). In the Node port this must be the basename of the script file ("test2.mjs"), substituted everywhere the reference prints "test2_executable": in the usage line, and as the "<prog>: error: " prefix.
findings.evidence: All usage/error lines observed as "usage: test2_executable [-h] --a A" and "test2_executable: error: ...".

findings.rule: USAGE = "usage: " + prog + " [-h] --a A\n". The required option --a appears WITHOUT square brackets; -h appears with them. Metavar is "A" (dest 'a' upper-cased).
findings.evidence: od -c of every error/help path begins `u s a g e :   t e s t 2 _ e x e c u t a b l e   [ - h ]   - - a   A \n` (35 bytes incl. newline).

findings.rule:
HELP (99 bytes with prog="test2_executable") = USAGE + "
" + "options:
" + "  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
" + "  --a A
". Note: header is "options:" (Python 3.10+ wording, not "optional arguments:"); exactly TWO spaces separate "-h, --help" from its help text (help column = 14 = 2 indent + 10 invocation width + 2 gap); the "--a A" line has no help text and therefore no trailing padding.
findings.evidence:
`-h` -> 99 stdout bytes; od -c shows `... - - a   A 
 
 o p t i o n s : 
     - h ,   - - h e l p     s h o w ...`. Byte math: 35+1+9+46+8 = 99.

findings.rule: Help is written to STDOUT and exits 0 with EMPTY stderr. It is never written to stderr.
findings.evidence: `test2_executable -h 2>&1 >/dev/null | od -c` -> 0 bytes. `-h` -> exit 0, stdout 99 / stderr 0.

findings.rule: Every error path writes NOTHING to stdout (0 bytes verified) and writes to stderr exactly USAGE + prog + ": error: " + MSG + "\n", then exits 2.
findings.evidence: All exit-2 cases report stdout_bytes=0. e.g. no-args -> 102 stderr bytes = 35 (usage) + 67 ("test2_executable: error: the following arguments are required: --a\n").

findings.rule: If --a was never successfully supplied, MSG = "the following arguments are required: --a".

If --a is present but the following token is absent or is classified as an option token, MSG = "argument --a: expected one argument". The reported name is the option string as typed is NOT used — it is always the canonical "--a".

MSG = "unrecognized arguments: " + extras.join(" ") — a SINGLE space between tokens, tokens emitted verbatim (including embedded spaces, which are therefore ambiguous) and in ORIGINAL argv order regardless of where they appeared relative to --a.
findings.evidence: [--a x extra1 extra2] -> "extra1 extra2"; [--a x extra1 extra2 extra3] -> "extra1 extra2 extra3"; [extra1 --a x extra2] -> "extra1 extra2"; [x y --a z] -> "x y"; [--b x --a y] -> "--b x"; [--a x y --a z] -> "y"; [--a x '-1 2'] -> "-1 2"; ['--foo bar' --a x] -> "--foo bar".

findings.rule: MSG = "ambiguous option: " + token + " could match " + matches.join(", ") where matches are the long options whose name starts with the prefix, in parser registration order (--help before --a). Reachable only via a token of the form "--=..." (prefix "--" matches both long options).
findings.evidence: [--=x] -> "ambiguous option: --=x could match --help, --a"; [--=] -> "ambiguous option: --= could match --help, --a".

findings.rule: MSG = "argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument " + pythonRepr(explicitArg). The action is named by its joined option strings "-h/--help". Python repr uses single quotes: 'x', '' for empty, '-x'. Triggered when the help action (nargs=0) is given an explicit value.
findings.evidence: [--help=x] and [--h=x] and [-h=1] -> "...ignored explicit argument 'x'" / "'1'"; [-h=] and [--help=] -> "...ignored explicit argument ''"; [-h-x] -> "...ignored explicit argument '-x'".

findings.rule: "--a=VALUE" assigns VALUE, splitting on the FIRST '=' only. "--a=" yields empty string (still counts as supplied, exit 0). The value after '=' is taken literally even if it looks like an option.

Unambiguous prefixes of long options are accepted (allow_abbrev default True): --h, --he, --hel, --help all invoke help. --a is matched exactly (it is also a prefix of nothing else). Any longer/other token is unknown: --aa, --A, --x, --xyz, --b are NOT matched to --a (abbreviation expands a prefix to a longer option, never the reverse), and matching is CASE-SENSITIVE.
findings.evidence: [--h], [--he], [--hel] -> help exit 0. [--aa x], [--A x], [--x], [--xyz] -> required-missing error (token treated as unknown option, discarded to extras).

findings.rule: For a single-dash token longer than 2 chars with no '=', argparse splits it as "-h" + tail. Since -h is nargs=0 and the tail's first char is not a prefix char, -h fires immediately (printing help and exiting 0) and the tail is never examined. So -hh, -hx, -hhh, -ha all print help, exit 0. If the first char does NOT match a known short option (-x, -xy, -xh) the whole token is unknown.
findings.evidence: [-hh], [-hx], [-hhh], [-ha] -> help exit 0. [-xh], [-xy], [-x] -> required-missing error.

findings.rule: The cluster path is taken ONLY when there was no '=' separator AND the tail does not begin with a prefix char ('-'). If an '=' was used, or the tail starts with '-', it is an explicit argument to a nargs=0 action -> "ignored explicit argument" error. Empty explicit arg ("-h=", "--help=") also errors.
findings.evidence: [-hx] -> help (cluster) vs [-h=1] -> ignored explicit argument '1' (sep '='); [-h-x] -> ignored explicit argument '-x' (tail starts with '-'); [-h=] / [--help=] -> ignored explicit argument ''.

findings.rule: A token exactly equal to "--" terminates option parsing: every token after it is forced to be a positional. Since this parser has NO positionals, all of them (and the "--" itself) become unrecognized extras. The "--" is NOT stripped — it appears verbatim in the unrecognized-arguments list.
findings.evidence: [--a x --] -> "unrecognized arguments: --"; [--a x -- extra] -> "-- extra"; [--a x -- --] -> "-- --"; [--a x -- -h] -> "-- -h" (note: -h after -- does NOT trigger help); [--a=x --] -> "--"; [--a x extra --] -> "extra --".

findings.rule: When "--" comes before --a, the --a token becomes a positional, so --a is never supplied and the required-missing error wins over unrecognized.
findings.evidence: [-- --a x], [-- -- --a x], [-- x], [-- -h], [--] -> "the following arguments are required: --a".

findings.rule: "--" can never be consumed as the value of --a; --a immediately followed by "--" errors with expected-one-argument (the separator is recognized before value consumption).
findings.evidence: [--a --] and [--a -- x] -> "argument --a: expected one argument".

findings.rule: Because no defined option looks like a negative number, a token matching the Python regex /^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$/ is treated as a VALUE (positional), not an option. Accepted as a value: -1, -0, -12345, -1.5, -.5, -0.5. NOT accepted (treated as option-like): -1e3, -1., -0x1, --1, -1.5.5, -+1, -1x, -x1. Note the regex requires at least one digit after the '.' and allows zero digits before it.
A standalone negative-number token is a positional, hence an unrecognized extra (or, if --a is missing, it triggers the required error).
findings.evidence: [-1] , [-1.5] -> required-missing; [-1 --a x] and [--a x -1] -> "unrecognized arguments: -1".

findings.rule: A token that contains a SPACE character (U+0020) anywhere is never treated as an option, even if it starts with '-' or '--'. It becomes a positional/value.
findings.evidence: [--a '-x y'] and [--a '--not an option'] and [--a '-1 '] -> exit 0 (accepted as values). ['--foo bar' --a x] -> "unrecognized arguments: --foo bar" (positional, not an unknown option). Note [--a ' -1'] is also a value, but for the simpler reason that its first char is not '-'.

findings.rule: An empty-string argv token is never an option; it is a positional. As a value of --a it is accepted (exit 0); standing alone it is an extra (required error fires first here).
findings.evidence: [--a ''] -> exit 0; [''] -> "the following arguments are required: --a".

findings.rule: A bare "-" (length 1) is never an option; it is a positional. Accepted as the value of --a; otherwise an unrecognized extra.
findings.evidence: [--a -] -> exit 0; [-] -> required-missing; [- --a x] and [--a x -] -> "unrecognized arguments: -".

findings.rule: Tokens like "---", "---a", "---help" are unknown options (prefix "---" matches no long option), discarded to extras.
findings.evidence: [---], [---a x], [---help] -> required-missing; [--a x ---] -> "unrecognized arguments: ---".

findings.rule: --a may be repeated; the last occurrence wins (store action overwrites). Output is unchanged since the value is unused. A trailing --a with no value still errors.
findings.evidence: [--a x --a y] and [--a x --a=y] -> exit 0; [--a x --a] and [--a=x --a] -> "expected one argument".

findings.rule: PRECEDENCE STEP 0 (highest): argparse classifies ALL argv tokens as option/positional in a left-to-right PRE-PASS before consuming anything. An 'ambiguous option' error raised during this pre-pass beats every other outcome, including expected-one-argument for an earlier --a, required-missing, and unrecognized.
findings.evidence: [--a --=x] -> "ambiguous option: --=x could match --help, --a" (NOT "expected one argument", which is what [--a --b] gives). [--=x] alone -> ambiguous, not required-missing. [--a x --=y], [--a=x --=] -> ambiguous.

findings.rule: PRECEDENCE STEP 1: the consumption pass runs left-to-right. The FIRST of {help action fires (print help, exit 0)} or {ArgumentError: expected-one-argument / ignored-explicit-argument} encountered wins, in argv order. Unknown options and stray positionals are silently deferred to extras during this pass and never interrupt it.
findings.evidence: [--a x -h extra] and [x -h] and [--b -h] and [-h --a] and [--help --a] and [-h ---] -> help exit 0 (the -h is reached without an earlier failure). [--a --b -h] and [--a -h x] -> "expected one argument" (the --a failure occurs first). [--help=x --a y] and [--a y --help=x] -> "ignored explicit argument 'x'" (beats both help and success).

findings.rule: PRECEDENCE STEP 2 then 3: after a clean consumption pass, the required-argument check runs BEFORE the unrecognized-arguments check. So if --a is missing, any extras are never reported.
findings.evidence: [--b x] , [--x], [-a x], [--A x], [--aa x], [-- x] -> "the following arguments are required: --a" even though extras exist. Only when --a IS supplied do extras surface: [--b x --a y] -> "unrecognized arguments: --b x".

findings.rule: An unknown long option written with '=' is kept as a single verbatim extra token; it is not split.
findings.evidence: [--a x --unknown=1] -> "unrecognized arguments: --unknown=1"; [--a=x --b=1] -> "unrecognized arguments: --b=1".

findings.rule: An unknown option does not swallow the token after it; both land in extras independently, preserving order.
findings.evidence: [--a x --b y] -> "unrecognized arguments: --b y"; [--b x --a y] -> "unrecognized arguments: --b x"; [--a x --A y] -> "unrecognized arguments: --A y".

findings.rule: type=str performs no conversion or validation. Values containing unicode, tabs, newlines, spaces, or leading '=' are all accepted verbatim with exit 0. There is no possible 'invalid str value' error.
findings.evidence: [--a 'héllo→'], [--a $'a\tb'], [--a $'a\nb'], [--a 'hello world'], [--a '=x'] -> exit 0, identical 43-byte stdout.

findings.rule: Usage and help are wrapped to (terminal width - 2), where width comes from the COLUMNS env var if set, else the tty size, else 80. With COLUMNS unset (the normal harness case) the layout is the 80-column one given above. Importantly, the "<prog>: error: MSG" line is NEVER wrapped, only the usage block is. A faithful port can hardcode width 80 unless it also intends to honor COLUMNS.
findings.evidence: COLUMNS=20 -> usage splits to "usage: test2_executable\n       [-h] --a A" and help text wraps, but the error line stays whole. COLUMNS=80/200 and unset -> identical 99-byte help.

result.notes:
Probes run against /workspace/dataset/test2_executable with stdout/stderr captured to separate files under /tmp/probe/out; harness at /tmp/probe/run.sh logs argv with printf '%q'. Source confirmed at /workspace/dataset/test2.py (the prompt's path /workspace/dataset/whoosh/test2.py does not exist).

Implementation summary for the Node port (prog = basename(scriptPath), e.g. "test2.mjs"):

USAGE  = `usage: ${prog} [-h] --a A\n`
HELP   = USAGE + `\noptions:\n  -h, --help  show this help message and exit\n  --a A\n`
OK     = `<Schema: ['id', 'price', 'tags', 'title']>\n`
FAIL(msg) -> stderr USAGE + `${prog}: error: ${msg}\n`, exit 2, stdout empty.

Algorithm:
1. classify(tok): returns OPTION or POSITIONAL.
   - "" -> POSITIONAL; tok[0] !== '-' -> POSITIONAL; tok === "-" -> POSITIONAL (len 1).
   - tok is exactly "-h" | "--help" | "--a" -> OPTION (exact).
   - if tok contains '=': split once; if left part is an exact option -> OPTION with sep='=' and explicitArg=right.
   - abbreviation: if tok starts with "--": prefix = part before '=' (or whole tok); collect long options starting with prefix; >1 -> ERROR `ambiguous option: ${tok} could match ${matches.join(', ')}` (order: --help, --a); ==1 -> OPTION.
     if tok starts with single '-': if tok.slice(0,2) is a known short option -> OPTION with sep='' and explicitArg=tok.slice(2).
   - if /^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$/.test(tok) -> POSITIONAL.
   - if tok includes ' ' -> POSITIONAL.
   - else OPTION (unknown -> goes to extras).
2. PRE-PASS over all tokens left-to-right doing classify(); the ambiguous error must be raised here, before any consumption. A token exactly "--" ends the pre-pass: it and everything after are POSITIONAL.
3. CONSUME left-to-right:
   - help option reached -> print HELP to stdout, exit 0. If it carries an explicitArg: when sep==='=' OR explicitArg starts with '-' OR explicitArg==='' -> FAIL(`argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument ${pyRepr(explicitArg)}`); otherwise ignore the tail and fire help.
   - "--a": if explicitArg present use it; else take the next token only if it is POSITIONAL, else FAIL("argument --a: expected one argument").
   - unknown option or stray positional -> push verbatim to extras, continue.
4. if --a never set -> FAIL("the following arguments are required: --a").
5. if extras.length -> FAIL("unrecognized arguments: " + extras.join(" ")).
6. else print OK, exit 0.

pyRepr(s) = "'" + s + "'" for all observed cases (no quotes/backslashes appeared in explicit args reachable here).

Watch-outs the port is easy to get wrong: (a) "--" is preserved verbatim in extras, not stripped; (b) required-check runs before unrecognized-check; (c) the ambiguous-option error fires in the pre-pass so it beats an earlier "--a expected one argument"; (d) "-hx" prints help while "-h=1" errors; (e) "-1"/"-.5" are values but "-1e3"/"-1." are not; (f) any token containing a space is never an option.
